#!/bin/bash

# Flux directives translated from SLURM
#FLUX: -N 1
#FLUX: -n 64
#FLUX: -c 1
#FLUX: -q c6gn
#FLUX: --exclusive
#FLUX: -o rfm_PismTest1_pism_1_1_4__gcc__cijv4kn___nodes___1___mpi___64___omp___1__job.out

#
# --- Omitted SLURM options and explanations ---
#
# --job-name=...
#   Omitted. The job name in Flux is generally set during submission (e.g.,
#   'flux submit --job-name=...') or via the FLUX_JOB_NAME
#   environment variable, not through a script directive.
#
# --error=...
#   Omitted. Flux combines stdout and stderr into the single output file
#   specified by the -o directive. To redirect stderr separately, you can use
#   shell redirection in your command, e.g., 'command 2> ...'.
#
# Note on memory:
#   The original SLURM script did not request a specific amount of memory. This job
#   will receive the default memory allocation from the scheduler, which could
#   be insufficient and lead to an out-of-memory error.
#

spack load pism@1.1.4 %gcc /cijv4kn
export OMP_NUM_THREADS=1
export OMP_PLACES=cores

# The SLURM 'srun' command is replaced by 'flux run'. 'flux run' will automatically
# launch the 64 tasks requested by the job directives.
flux run /usr/bin/time -f "real:%e" pismv -test B -Mx 61 -Mz 11 -ys 422.45 -y 25000 &> pismv.out

issues: The most significant resource-related issue is the lack of an explicit memory request. As noted in the comments, the original SLURM script also omitted this. For an MPI job using 64 cores, this is a critical omission. The job will receive a small, default memory allocation and is at high risk of failing with an out-of-memory error.

The script is missing a time limit (`-t`). While the original SLURM script also lacked one, this is poor practice. A hanging job could run indefinitely until a queue or system-wide limit is reached, wasting resources.

The script redirects the main application output to `pismv.out` while also specifying a job output file via `#FLUX: -o ...`. This can be confusing, as the primary job log specified by `-o` will not contain the application's verbose output, which will be in a different file.
